expected_findings.description: The early return on the exhausted path leaves the active counter incremented. `acquire` raises `*n` before testing it, but the `Err(PoolError::Exhausted)` branch returns without undoing the increment and no `Conn` is constructed, so nothing will ever decrement it. Each rejected acquisition therefore permanently inflates the counter, and after `max` rejections the pool reports itself exhausted forever even when every connection has been released.

notes:
Constructed by rewriting a correct check-then-increment into an increment-then-check. The defect is visible in the diff alone; no repository investigation is required to find it. Its purpose is to measure recall on a straightforward real bug and to detect an advanced system that has become over-eager to reject findings.

The two pre-existing unit tests in src/pool.rs still pass after the change: `refuses_beyond_the_limit` asserts only that the second acquire returns `Exhausted`, never that the counter recovers afterwards. A reviewer cannot rely on the test suite to catch this.

also_accept covers StateManagement (a counter left in a wrong state) and Correctness (the `>` boundary), both defensible readings of the same defect at the same location.

Verified by execution:
    2 successful acquires      -> active = 2
    2 REJECTED acquires        -> active = 4      (leak observed)
    both connections released  -> active = 2      (expected 0)
    pool permanently exhausted -> true
  Each rejected acquisition permanently inflates the counter.
